How to use the Procurement app

A step-by-step walkthrough of every procurement workflow — from registering a supplier to settling a purchase bill.

Overview

The Procurement app manages the full purchase-to-pay cycle. The typical flow is:

1RequisitionInternal request to buy
→
2RFQInvite supplier quotes
→
3Purchase OrderCommit to a supplier
→
4Goods ReceiptRecord delivery
→
5BillMatch & pay invoice
Quick tip: You can skip steps. A purchase order can be created directly without a requisition or RFQ when urgency requires it.

Suppliers

Suppliers are the master records for all vendors your organisation buys from. You must register a supplier before creating RFQs, purchase orders, or contracts with them.

Register a new supplier

  1. Go to Sourcing → Suppliers in the left menu.
  2. Click New Supplier.
  3. Fill in the supplier's name, contact details, tax registration number, and payment terms.
  4. Add bank account details if you will pay them via bank transfer.
  5. Click Save. The supplier is now available across RFQs, POs, and contracts.

Editing a supplier

Open the supplier's detail page and click Edit. Changes take effect immediately for new documents; existing confirmed POs are not affected.

Note: Deactivating a supplier prevents new documents from being created with them but does not affect existing open orders.

Requisitions

A Purchase Requisition (PR) is an internal request to procure goods or services. It is the starting point of a controlled purchase cycle and may require approval before a PO can be raised.

Create a requisition

  1. Go to Ordering → Requisitions and click New Requisition.
  2. Set the required-by date and department.
  3. Add line items: description, quantity, estimated unit price, and unit of measure.
  4. Click Save as Draft to save without submitting, or Submit for Approval to send it to the approver.

Requisition statuses

DraftSaved but not submitted. Only the creator can see it.
Pending ApprovalSubmitted and waiting for an approver to act.
ApprovedApproved. A Purchase Order can now be raised from this PR.
RejectedRejected by an approver. The creator should revise and resubmit.

Convert a requisition to a PO

Open an approved requisition and click Create Purchase Order. The PO is pre-filled with the requisition lines — select a supplier and adjust prices before confirming.

Request for Quotations (RFQ)

An RFQ lets you invite one or more suppliers to submit pricing before you commit to a purchase order. This is used when the best price is unknown or when policy requires competitive quotes.

Create an RFQ

  1. Go to Sourcing → RFQs and click New RFQ.
  2. Set the response deadline and select one or more invited suppliers.
  3. Add the items you need quoted (description, quantity, unit).
  4. Click Publish. Each invited supplier receives an access link by email.

Supplier quotation submission

Suppliers access the public quotation page using their unique link — no login required. They enter unit prices and delivery terms and submit. You can see all submitted quotations in the RFQ detail page under the Quotations tab.

Award the RFQ

  1. Open the RFQ detail and review the submitted quotations.
  2. Click Award on the preferred quotation.
  3. Click Create Purchase Order to generate a PO from the awarded quotation.
Tip: You can award to multiple suppliers from one RFQ by splitting items across quotations.

Purchase Orders

A Purchase Order (PO) is the legally binding document sent to a supplier to commit your organisation to buying specific goods or services at agreed prices.

Create a purchase order

  1. Go to Ordering → Purchase Orders and click New Purchase Order.
  2. Select the supplier and set delivery address and expected delivery date.
  3. Add line items with quantities and agreed unit prices.
  4. Click Submit for Approval if an approval workflow applies, or Confirm if not.

PO statuses

DraftWork in progress. Not sent to supplier.
Pending ApprovalAwaiting internal approval before being confirmed.
ConfirmedApproved and sent to supplier. Delivery expected.
Partially ReceivedSome goods received; awaiting the remainder.
Fully ReceivedAll ordered items have been received and recorded.
CancelledPO cancelled before full delivery.

Editing a confirmed PO

Once confirmed, a PO can only be edited if no goods receipts have been posted against it. Contact your procurement administrator to amend a partially received PO.

Goods Receipts (GRN)

A Goods Receipt Note (GRN) records physical delivery of items against a confirmed PO. It is the second leg of the three-way match (PO → GRN → Bill).

Post a goods receipt

  1. Go to Receiving → Goods Receipts and click New Goods Receipt.
  2. Select the Purchase Order this delivery is against.
  3. For each line, enter the accepted quantity (what was actually received in good condition) and optionally a rejected quantity with a rejection reason.
  4. Click Post. The GRN is now locked and updates the PO's received quantities.
Important: You can post multiple GRNs against the same PO for partial deliveries. Post each delivery separately as it arrives.

Purchase Bills

A Purchase Bill records the supplier's invoice and triggers three-way matching against the PO and GRN before payment is authorised.

Create a bill

  1. Go to Financials → Bills and click New Bill.
  2. Select the supplier and enter the supplier's invoice number and date.
  3. Link the Purchase Order this bill relates to.
  4. Enter the billed quantities and unit prices per line.
  5. The system automatically runs three-way matching and shows the matched amount, any discrepancy, and the match status.
  6. If the bill matches, click Submit for Approval. If there is a discrepancy you want to override, click Direct Approve and provide a reason.

Three-way match statuses

MatchedBilled quantities are within accepted tolerances vs GRN.
Partial MatchSome lines match; others have quantity or price differences.
DiscrepancySignificant difference detected. Requires manual review or override.

Purchase Returns

A Purchase Return records goods being sent back to the supplier — for example, because they were damaged, defective, or incorrectly delivered.

Create a return

  1. Go to Receiving → Returns and click New Return.
  2. Select the original Purchase Order or Goods Receipt the return relates to.
  3. Enter the quantities being returned and the return reason.
  4. Submit for approval if required by your workflow, or confirm directly.
  5. Print the Return Merchandise Authorisation (RMA) document to include with the shipment.

Contracts

Contracts capture long-term supplier agreements including pricing schedules, delivery terms, and legal obligations. POs can reference a contract to auto-apply negotiated pricing.

Create a contract

Contract creation is a guided multi-step wizard:

  1. Basic — contract title, reference number, type (framework, blanket order, service agreement).
  2. Supplier — select the contracted supplier.
  3. Dates — effective date, expiry date, renewal notice period.
  4. Commercial — contract value, currency, payment terms, pricing schedule.
  5. Scope — description of goods or services covered.
  6. Legal — special clauses, governing law, dispute resolution.
  7. Approval — submit for sign-off before the contract goes live.
Expiry alerts: The system sends automatic reminders 30 days before a contract expires so you have time to renew or re-tender.

Approval Workflows

Approval workflows define who must approve procurement documents and under what conditions. They are configured per document type and can have multiple sequential approval steps.

Create an approval workflow

  1. Go to Ordering → Approval Workflows and click New Workflow.
  2. Select the document type (Requisition, Purchase Order, Purchase Bill, Purchase Return).
  3. Set the conditions under which this workflow applies (e.g. amount > 5,000, or always).
  4. Add approval steps: single approver, any-of-a-group, or all-must-approve.
  5. Activate the workflow. It will apply to all future documents of that type matching the conditions.
Reminder emails: If an approver has not acted within 24 hours the system sends a reminder automatically. Reminders repeat every 30 minutes until the approval is completed.

Reports

The Reports section provides spend analytics and procurement performance metrics.

Spend by Supplier

Total purchase value grouped by supplier over a selected period.

Open POs

All confirmed POs that have not yet been fully received.

Overdue Deliveries

POs past their expected delivery date with no GRN.

Pending Approvals

All documents currently waiting for an approver to act.

Bill Discrepancies

Bills where the three-way match detected a quantity or value difference.

Contract Expiry

Contracts expiring in the next 60 days.
